The motivation is the R4 risk row in\ndesign-spec §10: a fan-out of 15 concurrent HOMEs with PTY transcripts\ncan grow past several hundred megabytes on a slow eval; left unchecked,\nthat fills the developer host (or a CI runner with a tight disk quota)\nand corrupts every neighbouring run. The orchestrator addresses this\nby polling the run-directory size every five seconds and signalling a\n\"stop scheduling, drain in-flight, exit 2\" breach when the configured\nbudget is exceeded.\n\nThis module implements the polling primitive. The integration with\n:class:`RunOrchestrator` lives in ``orchestrator.py``; the CLI flag\n(``--max-disk-mb``) is wired by the Phase 4 dispatcher per design-spec\n§4. The poller is deliberately decoupled from both so it can be exercised\nin isolation by the T03.19 fixture suite (``test_disk_budget.py``) and\nre-used by any future component (eg. the doctor pre-flight) that needs\na cheap, side-effect-free disk gauge.\n\nPublic surface\n==============\n\n:class:`DiskBudgetPoller`\n    Background-thread poller. Constructed with an output directory and a\n    ``max_disk_mb`` budget; ``start()`` / ``stop()`` (or the context-\n    manager form) drive the background thread. Exposes :meth:`is_breached`\n    so the orchestrator can short-circuit its submission loop and\n    :meth:`breach_detail` for the partial-summary payload.\n\n:data:`DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE`\n    Process exit code emitted by the Phase 4 dispatcher when the poller\n    has flagged a breach. ``2`` per design-spec §4 (harness error).\n\n:data:`DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`\n    Filename of the side-car the poller writes inside the run directory\n    on breach. The Reporter (COMP-008 / T03.13) surfaces this path under\n    ``RunSummary.artifacts['disk_budget_exceeded']``; the filename is\n    pinned here so consumers do not have to discover it by scan.\n\nBreach semantics\n================\n\nWhen ``max_disk_mb > 0``:\n\n* The poller measures cumulative size of the output directory tree every\n  ``tick_sec`` seconds (default ``5.0``). The first tick fires *after*\n  the initial sleep so an empty run directory does not get flagged on\n  start-up.\n* When measured usage exceeds ``max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`` bytes, the\n  poller writes ``DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`` into the output\n  directory, sets its internal ``is_breached()`` flag, and exits the\n  loop. The flag is one-shot — once set, the poller stays in the\n  breached state for the rest of its lifetime.\n* The orchestrator polls ``is_breached()`` between submissions; on a\n  breach it stops scheduling new specs and synthesises a\n  ``SKIPPED`` outcome (skip_reason ``\"disk_budget_exceeded\"``) for every\n  unsubmitted spec. In-flight workers continue to completion — the\n  poller never kills a thread or sends a signal.\n\nWhen ``max_disk_mb == 0``:\n\n* The poller is *disabled*. ``start()`` is a no-op, the background\n  thread is never spawned, and :meth:`is_breached` always returns\n  ``False``. The orchestrator behaves as if no poller were wired.\n  Design-spec §4 documents ``--max-disk-mb 0`` as the \"disable\"\n  invocation.\n\nThread safety\n=============\n\nThe breach state is stored as a :class:`threading.Event`. Reading the\ndetail mapping after :meth:`is_breached` returns ``True`` is safe because\nthe detail is published *before* the event is set (release-then-set\nordering). Already-running workers observe\n                    # the token themselves (via :class:`EvalRunner`) and\n                    # convert to INTERRUPTED outcomes; we synthesise an\n                    # INTERRUPTED row for every spec that did not even\n                    # reach the pool so the per-spec contract still holds.\n                    #\n                    # Cancellation is checked *before* the disk-budget\n                    # breach so a SIGINT received concurrently with a\n                    # breach routes the spec to INTERRUPTED (operator\n                    # intent dominates a resource limit).\n                    if self._is_cancelled():\n                        cancelled_indices.append(index)\n                        continue\n                    if self._is_disk_budget_exceeded():\n                        disk_budget_skipped_indices.append(index)\n                        continue\n                    future = pool.submit(self._invoke_worker, spec)\n                    futures[future] = index\n\n                # Drain the pool. ``as_completed`` is the AC6 idiom — it\n                # yields each future the instant its worker returns,\n                # letting downstream readers (telemetry, TUI) update in\n                # near real-time without waiting for the slowest eval.\n                # In-flight workers continue to completion even after a\n                # disk-budget breach — the AC6 contract requires \"in-\n                # flight evals complete\" before the run exits.\n                for future in as_completed(futures):\n                    index = futures[future]\n                    spec = specs[index]\n                    try:\n                        outcomes[index] = future.result()\n                    except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — see docstring\n                        # The worker should fold its own harness errors\n                        # into an ERRORED outcome via :func:`run_eval`. We\n                        # only get here when the worker itself raised\n                        # (construction failure, unwired-token\n                        # KeyboardInterrupt propagation, etc.). Translate\n                        # to ERRORED so :meth:`run` never re-raises.\n                        outcomes[index] = self._errored_outcome(spec, exc)\n        finally:\n            if poller is not None:\n                poller.stop()\n\n        # Backfill INTERRUPTED outcomes for never-submitted specs after\n        # the pool has shut down so we cannot race with an in-flight\n        # cancellation.\n        for index in cancelled_indices:\n            outcomes[index] = self._interrupted_outcome(specs[index])\n        # Backfill SKIPPED outcomes for specs we declined to submit\n        # because the disk budget was breached. The optional ``signum_holder``\n    attribute records the signal number that triggered cancellation so\n    downstream consumers can include it in the partial summary.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    __slots__ = (\"_event\", \"_signum\", \"_signum_lock\")\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self._event = threading.Event()\n        self._signum: Optional[int] = None\n        self._signum_lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def cancel(self, *, signum: Optional[int] = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Flip the token to the cancelled state.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        signum:\n            Optional signal number that caused the cancellation. Stored\n            on the token so the orchestrator / reporter can record\n            ``\"interrupted_by\"`` in the partial summary. Only the first\n            ``cancel()`` call captures the signum; subsequent calls\n            return ``False`` without overwriting.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        bool\n            ``True`` if this call was the one that flipped the flag,\n            ``False`` if the token was already cancelled. Lets the\n            orchestrator distinguish \"I cancelled\" from \"I observed\n            an already-cancelled token\" without racing against a\n            second signal.\n        \"\"\"\n        first = not self._event.is_set()\n        if first:\n            with self._signum_lock:\n                if not self._event.is_set():\n                    if signum is not None:\n                        self._signum = int(signum)\n                    self._event.set()\n                else:\n                    first = False\n        return first\n\n    def is_cancelled(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return ``True`` once the token has been cancelled.\"\"\"\n        return self._event.is_set()\n\n    def wait(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Block until cancelled or ``timeout`` elapses.\n\n        Returns ``True`` if the token is cancelled when the call\n        returns, ``False`` on timeout. Matches the\n        :meth:`threading.Event.wait` contract so callers familiar with\n        ``Event`` semantics need no adapter.\n        \"\"\"\n        return self._event.wait(timeout)\n\n    @property\n    def signum(self) -> Optional[int]:\n        \"\"\"The signal number that caused cancellation, if any.\"\"\"\n        with self._signum_lock:\n            return self._signum\n\n\n# Signal-handler callback signature: ``(signum, frame, token)`` — matches\n# the stdlib :class:`signal.signal` callback plus the token so callers\n# can implement extra bookkeeping (partial-summary writing, telemetry)\n# without keeping a global token reference.\nOnSignalCallback = Callable[[int, Optional[FrameType], \"CancellationToken\"], None]\n\n\nclass SignalHandlerInstaller:\n    \"\"\"Context manager binding ``SIGINT``/``SIGTERM`` to a cancellation token.\n\n    On ``__enter__`` the installer registers a handler for each signal","numLines":90,"startLine":50,"totalLines":255}}}

May be\\n      empty for partial summaries written on SIGINT before the\\n      orchestrator completed.\\n    * ``duration_sec``     — wall-clock seconds the orchestrator ran end\\n      to end. ``float`` for sub-millisecond resolution.\\n    * ``suite``            — manifest path / suite identifier the\\n      orchestrator loaded. The Reporter renders this verbatim in the\\n      summary header.\\n    * ``manifest_version`` — semantic version stamped on the manifest at\\n      author time. Helps the Reporter detect mismatched evals when a\\n      manifest is bumped between runs.\\n    * ``parallel``         — concurrency level the orchestrator scheduled\\n      at (post-clamp to ``[1,15]``). The Reporter surfaces this so\\n      reviewers can correlate the wall-clock budget against the scheduler\\n      knob.\\n    * ``counts``           — ``RunCounts`` instance (DM-012 counts sub-\\n      structure). ``__post_init__`` asserts the\\n      ``kept_k + skipped_s == expanded_n_prime`` equation matches the\\n      ``kept_plus_skipped_equals_n_prime`` flag; mismatched counts raise\\n      ``ValueError`` so a misreporting orchestrator fails loudly.\\n    * ``totals``           — ``RunTotals`` instance (DM-012 totals sub-\\n      structure). The 6 status tallies the Reporter renders in the\\n      summary headline.\\n    * ``evals``             — tuple of ``EvalOutcome`` records (DM-001 /\\n      T03.01), one per expanded spec. Stored as a tuple so the frozen\\n      dataclass preserves equality and hashability. FR-RPT1 (T03.11)\\n      enforces ``len(evals) == counts.expanded_n_prime`` *outside* this\\n      model so partial summaries (SIGINT) can still be constructed for\\n      writing.\\n    * ``artifacts``        — mapping of artifact-name to absolute (or\\n      run-relative) path produced by the orchestrator (e.g. the JSONL\\n      directory, the disk-budget breach side-car). Stored as an immutable\\n      ``Mapping`` so the frozen dataclass keeps its hashability contract;\\n      ``to_dict()`` returns a shallow copy so callers that mutate the\\n      returned mapping do not affect the immutable source.\\n\\n    Field declaration order matches DM-004 verbatim (see\\n    ``_RUN_SUMMARY_FIELDS``) so ``to_dict()`` output is stable across\\n    Reporter snapshots and review diffs.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n    run_id: str\\n    started_at: str\\n    finished_at: str\\n    duration_sec: float\\n    suite: str\\n    manifest_version: str\\n    parallel: int\\n    counts: RunCounts\\n    totals: RunTotals\\n    evals: tuple[EvalOutcome, ...] = ()\\n    artifacts: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)\\n\\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\\n        # DM-012 declares ``kept_plus_skipped_equals_n_prime`` as the\\n        # boolean assertion that the equation holds. Nested ``RunCounts`` / ``RunTotals`` / ``EvalOutcome``\\n        values are unwrapped via their own ``to_dict()`` so the Reporter\\n        never has to recurse manually. ``artifacts`` is shallow-copied\\n        into a plain ``dict`` so callers that mutate the returned mapping\\n        do not affect the immutable source.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n        payload: dict[str, Any] = {}\\n        for name in _RUN_SUMMARY_FIELDS:\\n            value = getattr(self, name)\\n            if name in (\\\"counts\\\", \\\"totals\\\"):\\n                payload[name] = value.to_dict()\\n            elif name == \\\"evals\\\":\\n                payload[name] = [item.to_dict() for item in value]\\n            elif name == \\\"artifacts\\\":\\n                payload[name] = dict(value)\\n            else:\\n                payload[name] = value\\n        return payload\"}]"}}}
